checkpoints.description: [1/1] Pin concurrent requests to stay clean

impact_assessment.why: the cockpit runs on a threaded HTTP server while a ticker thread ticks and autosaves, so parallel requests are a real path, yet no test had ever issued them; a race would surface as a 500, a corrupt save or a half-applied mutation
impact_assessment.benefits: the threaded path gains a regression test inside the normal suite and a wide probe gives confidence beyond it
impact_assessment.risks: contract: test-only; dependency: none; concurrency: the test itself issues parallel requests and joins with a timeout; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: two-thread server test asserting no 5xx, valid JSON, sane state and a successful step afterwards, plus a 480-request eight-thread probe

checkpoints.description: [1/1] Concurrency test passes in 0.66s inside the 60-test server suite; 480-request probe: 0 server errors, 0 transport errors, 0 bad state, finite payload, no negative populations; suite Ran 2204 OK; 6/6 project gates (ADR-423); checklists: passed
Task 'concurrent-requests' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/1] Credit escort achievements by commission, not current roster

impact_assessment.why: a full campaign left escort/squadron/fleet_captain/captain_corps at zero after commissioning, captaining and fighting a corvette, because the metrics read the live roster and the post-story decommission (ADR-402) emptied it; any player who sells or loses an escort would lose the achievement
impact_assessment.benefits: fleet achievements become monotonic lifetime events, with the live roster kept as a floor so old saves still read correctly
impact_assessment.risks: contract: codex metric semantics change additively, metrics keep live-roster floor; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: one new stats counter for captain assignments
impact_assessment.mitigation: seven failing-first tests for commission, sale, dismissal, recall, repeated commissions, legacy floor and higher-of, plus the 180 gate and seed-42 campaign

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Rebuild devastated worlds with relief supplies

impact_assessment.why: the AI only used credit reconstruction, so the relief branch (medicines/hydroponics/fuel cell, 40 devastation, +5 standing) had no campaign proof and relief_deliveries never moved; worlds_rebuilt also ignored relief landings
impact_assessment.benefits: the captain lands relief when already docked with stockable bags, rebuilding twice as much devastation for more standing, then falls back to credits away from a dock
impact_assessment.risks: contract: _reconstruct_action gains a bounded stocking step and the worlds_rebuilt metric adds relief landings; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: no schema change
impact_assessment.mitigation: nine failing-first tests for supply preference, stocking order and bound, undocked credit fallback, intact systems and the shared recipe; all three benchmark campaigns re-measured

checkpoints.description: [2/2] The vent policy honours the coolant it can read

impact_assessment.why: the top-level reactor snapshot never exposed last_vent_tick or can_vent, so the vent policy read -1 and posted the purge every step while a core stayed hot: 1,636 of 1,654 campaign refusals were the recharging refusal
impact_assessment.benefits: the cooldown gate works, refusals return to 20 on seed 1, and the purge stays the deliberate emergency action
impact_assessment.risks: contract: the snapshot gains two additive fields; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: five failing-first tests for the snapshot fields, fresh/recharged cooldown, first vent and a real engine vent
